events.title: Venezuela Brazil currency-control closure December 2016
events.direction: Initial report describes all passage at the crossing; December 20 pedestrian release in both directions and Brazilian vehicle return into Brazil.
events.movement: Persons and vehicles at the named crossing according to Brazilian MRE; later pedestrian and registered Brazilian return phases differed.
events.exceptions: Registered Brazilian vehicle returns began December 19, with a 14h window and prior registration; pedestrian traffic in both directions released December 20.
events.enforcement: Brazilian consulate/MRE reported the Venezuelan gate closure from December 13. Documented Brazilian returns began December 19 before broader pedestrian release December 20.
events.relationship: Brazil-crossing implementation related to AM010 currency policy, not an additive independent national decision.
events.status_observation: Evidence dated in cited sources; no assumption of present status.
events.official_rationale: Prevent movement of withdrawn 100 bolivar banknotes.
events.uncertainty: Onset now supported as December 13 by a contemporary official report. December 20 is a pedestrian phase endpoint, not first passage or total reopening. A retrospective indexed IPEA passage gives January 6 reopening; full scope could not be inspected. Do not bridge December 19/20 openings into a single universal closed spell.

events.direction: Canada-bound interval; US-bound access restored by February 8.
events.movement: Canada-bound passenger and commercial traffic through Ambassador Bridge; initial disruption also affected US-bound traffic.
events.exceptions: US-bound commercial traffic could use surface-street access from February 8; emergency access and diversion via other crossings existed.
events.enforcement: Policy or report as cited; uniform implementation at every crossing not presumed.
events.status_observation: Evidence dated in cited sources; no assumption of present status.
events.official_rationale: Protest opposition to pandemic restrictions; CBSA suspended unsafe or inaccessible service.
events.context: Non-state blockade, distinct from government public-health border order.
events.uncertainty: CBSA service-resumption message 00:11 ET February 14 defines endpoint for Canada-bound processing. US-bound access was restored by February 8, so the interval must not be read as continuous bidirectional closure. RCMP NATTERJACK instead places full bridge reopening late on February13; physical reopening versus CBSA message timing remains unresolved.

historical.duration_note: No exact interval: RCMP places reopening late February13 while CBSA service-resumption message is February14 00:11 ET.

claim_checks.Historical note — current findings are i: Deliberate Canada-bound access blockade confirmed.
February7 20:59 CBSA suspension; prior slow rolls excluded.
CBSA February14 00:11 message versus RCMP February13 late-night opening.

Hierarchical coding: see Rationale coding for subcategories, attribution and phases. The protest opposed pandemic rules. CBSA also suspended service because access was unsafe or obstructed. Infection control was not the blockade's purpose. Prior evidence assessment (before this recoding): Pandemic/public-health mandates were the protest issue; no event-specific evidence supports Elite politics. The retained Public health label describes issue context, not government infection-control purpose.
Canada-bound services; US-bound access remained possible.
New contrary operational date prevents exact physical interval; retain message date but remove interval.

duration_periods.display: Formal policy: confirmed through 2026-09-03; at least 2360 calendar-day difference; reopening unknown
duration_periods.scope: Ordinary non-permitted foreign road entry into mainland Azerbaijan across the Georgia, Russia and Iran frontiers; freight and individually authorised entry excluded.
duration_periods.basis: The mainland passenger restrictions were introduced by frontier: Iran on February 29, Georgia on March 14, and Russia on March 18, 2020. These dates bound commencement across the retained road-entry scope. The September 3, 2026 consular notice confirms continued ordinary-entry restrictions, subject to the separately documented rail and Nakhchivan exceptions.
duration_periods.qualification: Nakhchivan–Turkey phases and Georgia passenger rail reopening are excluded. The September Czech page's all-land wording conflicts with Azerbaijan's specific rail permission from 25 May 2026 and documented 26 May outward train. Exit rules differ; no post-3 September persistence inferred.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Intentional Thai passenger restrictions and the Sadao pilot occurred. The parent remains included; the proposal changes duration eligibility, not occurrence. The parent is a national umbrella, but the timed phase concerns ordinary non-repatriation passenger admission at Sadao. Freight, screened drivers and limited Thai returns are exceptions. The observed endpoint cannot be transferred to all Thai land borders. Restrictions were in place by 23 March 2020 and earlier local measures are evidenced. The first Sadao denial for the selected cohort is not directly dated. Propose withholding a complete operational duration while retaining the observed 1 April 2022 pilot endpoint and the by-23-March marker. Health and biosecurity / Human disease control is explicitly supported by the relayed official pandemic purpose. Other reasons are not inferred. Bernama diplomatic reporting, local pilot reporting, a later official MFA briefing and the earlier Xinhua report were read. The original Songkhla article and IOM PDF failed; an attributed indexed reproduction is identified as such. The phase is unlocated. Nong Khai reporting concerns Laos, not Cambodia. Proposed descriptive examples use freshly inspected evidence without making new geometry claims or treating national permission as opposite-side operation.
